title: Task Relay Item List Schema v1.3
description: JSON schema for task-relay item-list.json file

description.description: Brief description of what the assignment accomplishes

created.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when assignment was created

last_updated.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when assignment was last updated

next_override.description: Set to an item ID to override the selection algorithm. Cleared (set to null) only when the user confirms and the item is marked in_progress.

category.description: Category for grouping (e.g., setup, implementation, testing)

description.description: Clear, actionable description of what needs to be done

validation_steps.description: Item-level rollup validation steps (all tasks completed + end-to-end checks)

status.description: Current status of the item. blocked = not terminal; cancelled = terminal (notes required)

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when item reached terminal status (null if not terminal)

notes.description: Additional context or blocker info. REQUIRED when status == cancelled.

working_dir.description: Path to per-item working folder (e.g. 20-working/ITEM-001). Null/absent until item first transitions to in_progress.

files.description: Files inside working_dir, agent-maintained. OUTPUT of the work (compare `context`, the input).

rulebook.description: Optional path (relative to the project root) of this item's rulebook: objective, deliverables, acceptance, boundaries, stop. Every task of the item reads it before work and checks it before closing. Usually 20-working/<ITEM-ID>/<ITEM-ID>-rulebook.md.

context.description: Optional paths (relative to the project root) that every task of this item must read before work. INPUT to the work; not checked at closing (compare `files`, the output).

tasks.description: Ordered list of tasks for this item. Every item has at least one task.

id.description: Task identifier e.g. TASK-001-01. Embeds item number for machine-obvious linkage.

status.description: Task status. blocked = not terminal; cancelled = terminal (notes required)

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when task reached terminal status

notes.description: Additional context. REQUIRED when status == cancelled.

rulebook.description: Optional path (relative to the project root) of this task's rulebook. Read before work, on resume after a handoff and after compaction; checked before closing. Usually 20-working/<ITEM-ID>/<TASK-ID>-rulebook.md. The task also uses its item's rulebook.

context.description: Optional paths (relative to the project root) that only this task must read before work. Not checked at closing. The task also reads its item's context.

blocker.description: Optional blocker record (D6). Only set while the task status is `blocked`. Required when the task is blocked and the cause is known: `type` and `summary` and `since` are always present, plus `question` for type `needs_user` or `waiting_on` for type `external`. Remove the whole object when the task leaves `blocked` (for example when the user answers or the external dependency clears).

type.description: Who or what can clear the blocker. needs_user = only the user can answer or decide; external = an outside system, person, or event must act.

summary.description: One short line naming what is blocked.

question.description: The question the agent needs the user to answer. REQUIRED when type == needs_user.

default_action.description: Optional suggested action to take if the user does not answer. Advice only; the agent still stops and asks (D7).

waiting_on.description: What the task is waiting for. REQUIRED when type == external.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the task first became blocked by this cause.

terminal_summary.description: Compact summaries of terminal items (completed or cancelled). Full records in item-list-archive.json.

id.description: Item identifier matching the original item

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when item became terminal

total_items.description: Total number of items. Must equal sum of all status counts.

in_progress.description: Number of items in progress (0 or 1)
